HYDERABAD DISTRICT
Hyderabad.—Impression and photo-print of copper-plates in the possession of the Director of Archaeology and Museums, Hyderabad. Through Dr. G. S. Gai.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Records that the chief granted the royal insignia and the city Krivvaka in Viṣṇu-nūḍu as an agrahāra on the occasion of śrīkaraṇamu Indapariju and his brother Rāmanāyu, sons of Āyitana-nāyu, belonging to the Kamma-kula, for their loyalty, after their hereditary wealth (kuladhanamutu), their own territory viz., Viṣṇu-nūḍu and all their belongings and had also suffered for 12 years along with those of the king in the battle of Mudugonda. This is dated in the first regnal year of the chief. It is also stated that Kuriyagonneḍu, the lord of Koravipura restored Kusumāyudha. The genealogy of the king is given. In characters of about the 11th century.

GUJARAT
AHMEDABAD DISTRICT
Ahmedabad.—Copper-plates in the possession of the Director of Archaeology, Gujarat.
cells.remarks: Issued from Mānyakhēṭa. Gives the genealogy of the king and records the grant of the village Ānanda situated in the Lāṭa-dēśa, belonging to Bhaṭṭa Lāḍaiya, son of Bhaṭṭa Nāgadēva, who hailed from Pauṇḍrapura-sthāna and was well-versed in the four Vēdas and belonged to the Hārīta-gōtra and was also a student of the Vājasanēya-śākhā. The dūtaka of the record was Nāyēraka-purōhita and the writer was Mahāsāndhivigrahika Haragaṇpa, son of Nāṇṇa. Published in the Journal of Oriental Institute, Baroda, Vol. XX, No. 2, pp. 165 ff.

cells.place: Same plate, reverse
cells.remarks: Registers the exemption of tax on the tax, a vaḍḍa levied on the property in Hebbaḷe by the chief at the request of the same pontiff mentioned in No. 13 above for facilitating the charities in the maṭha. The tax is said to have been granted in Toḷagere. The levy (1 varāha) on the property was stated to have been made when it was leased, earlier by the palace to Malli-soṭṭi, son of Nāgappa-soṭṭi of Coreso e who at that time was given to him, but later, the same was stated to have been given to the same pontiff mentioned above.

cells.place: No. 10
cells.remarks: Refers to the chief's rule over Nagire, Hāḍu, Tuḷu, Konkaṇa etc. Records that since, Rāma Heggāḍe and Liṅga Heggāḍe misappropriated the lands belonging to the Śāntikadēvi temple, the ārādhana of the temple had ceased. After settlement the income from the lands was handed over to Rāmachandra-tirtha-śrīpādangaḷu as the maṭh of the temple lands with the stipulation that the income from 1/4 of the lands should be remitted to the royal treasury.

UTTAR PRADESH—concld.
LUCKNOW DISTRICT
LUCKNOW TAHSIL
Lucknow.—Photographs of a copper-plate charter received from Dr. N. P. Joshi, Director, State Museum.
cells.remarks: Issued from his victorious camp at Śrī-Muḍgagiri. Records the grant of two villages Aṅgāragartikā in Krauñcha-dhānaka-viṣaya in Śrīnagara-bhukti and Vasantikā in the same viṣaya, to the temple of Mahā-Vasantikā-bhaṭṭārikā and two villages, Kulaputraka in Dēvarāṣṭra-viṣaya and Navallikā in Kalmashaṇāśapāra-viṣaya to Śaivāchārya-parishad to be enjoyed permanently at the hands of the queen, the mother of the ruling king. The dēśaka of the record was Balavarmmā and the charter was engraved by Sāmanta Dāmodara and Vārchahadāsa. Noticed in Bulletin of Museums and Archaeology in U. P., June-December 1970, Nos. 5-6, pages 67-70.

cells.place: Stone pillar lying in a field outside the village.
cells.date: Śaka 1112 (dina- Vaiśākha śu. 11 (rudra) Wednesday = 1190 A.D., April 18. (The cyclic year was Sādhāraṇa).
cells.remarks: Records that Nṛisiṁha of Madhunikāpurī situated in Nāṭāḍi (Nāṭavāḍi) and Nāgāṁbā of Divya-vaṁśa and grandson of Narasiṁha and Nāgāṁbā, consecrated (the images of) Sambhu and Viṣṇu and appointed Sāntadēva, a Śiva-vipra, for their worship and for the protection of the temple. It is also stated to have made endowment of 2 khaṇḍikas of land to the deities and 2 drōṇas of land probably to Sāntadēva. Cf. Hyd. Arch. Series, No. 19, No. Km. 11, pp. 23 ff.; Tēlangāṇa Śāsanamu, Vol. I, No. 10, pp. 168 ff.

cells.location: Māgūru
cells.place: Stone pillar set up by the side of the Sītārāmasvāmī temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged at the beginning. Records the construction of the Trikuṭa temples of Kēśavadēva, Sūryadēva and probably of Mallikārjuna-mahādēva. Also records the endowment of (one) maṭha on north side of the village and the trees and the other containing 100 kuntas of land. On the east and south of the temples respectively for worship and food-offerings (havi-bali-archana) of the deities and the village-officers on the north of the village and the quarters for the mahājanas to the east of the temple. Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāya Nummadi Duggarāju is stated to have endowed 3 acres of wet-land behind the tank and 3 puttis of land on the western bank of the tank-bank for the worship and food-offerings of Kallikārjuna-mahādēva of the Trikuṭa temples. Do.

cells.place: Chhatri containing footprints, on the roadside near Dharmagira-kī-Talaiyā.
cells.date:
(1) Vikrama 1823, Māgha ba 5.
(2) Vikrama 1837
(3) Vikrama [1911], Pausha śu 13.
cells.remarks: In three portions. The first portion, in the front, records the death of Muto Bāsha(kha) tamalaji, the son of Muto Chunnamaji mahājana (i.e. a merchant) on the first date and the construction of the chhatri on the date. The second portion, to the right of the footprint, records the renovation probably of the chhatri, on the third date by Lālābhūdana. The third portion on the other one, some of which belonged to Gwalior State, gives details of the size of the footprints, records that the chhatri was constructed on the bank of the tank on the field belonging to Gusainī Rājachandra and Dīvānajī by Rūpachandra. Dīvānajī chandra when Ousahi Rājyams was the pontiff. The masons were Bālākisana and Gamgārāma. For the first portion Cf. ibid., No. 512.

Dīvānajī chandra when Ousahi Rājyams was the pontiff. The masons were Bālākisana and Gamgārāma. For the first portion Cf. ibid., No. 512.Read more (1 KB)

cells.location: Rāmāpur

cells.date: Śaka 1073, Pramādi, Bhādrapada Paurṇamī, Friday, lunar eclipse, 1150 A.D., September 8.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the chief and registers the grant of land measuring 4 nivartanas measured by Kīmḍidēśa-daṇḍa, a garden at the village of Rāmāpura, to the basadi at the same place as the village of Maḍalūra for the worship (ashṭa-vidhārcchana) and for the repairs and renovation of the Pārśvanātha temple which was built by Chaudhare Kāma-dēva. The gift was entrusted to the āchārya of the basadi, Siddhāntadēva, the disciple of Māghanandi-siddhāntadēva-dēva-tho āchārya of the Rūpanārāyaṇa-chaityālaya at Kshulla-kapura (Kolhāpura). Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXII, pp. 211 ff.

cells.date: Chālukya, Vikrama [50], Viśvāvasu, Vaiśākha śu. 3, (akshaya tr̥itīyā), [1125 A.D., April 8.
cells.remarks: Partly worn out. Records the release of 80 mattar of land, 12 mattar of garden and 2 house-sites, belonging to the deity Rāmadēvadēva of Muchahalunhi which were kept in pledge (guṇḍi) by the guruvu, on being persuaded by the Mahājanas, Aliyabali-gāvunḍa, etc., with all the āruvaṇas by the nunneyaas, grant of other gifts by the same etc., for the purpose of perpetual lamp, raṅgabhōga, etc., and also the gift and renovation in the temple of the deity and of 1 māru for the priest who was reciting the purāṇa in the agniśthage-maṭha in the same place. Refers to ...nayya-danḍanāyaka as one of the donors.

cells.remarks: Refers to the Jaina pontiffs Prabhāchandra-traividya- bhaṭṭāraka, Rāmachandramuni and [his] disciple Bālachandramuni. It states that the oil-mill of the basadi for the purpose of the daily worship and the special worship on the days of Jīvadayāshṭamī, Nandīvardhanāshṭa- mī, saṅkramaṇa and grahaṇa, and for Renovation. Pub- lished in Jainism in South India, pp. 259 ff.

cells.place: SHAMPUR TALUK
cells.date: Regnal year 2, Hēmalambi, Sunday, Vyātipāta, Uttarāyana-saṅkrānti=1168 A.D., December 27.
cells.remarks: Indifferently engraved. Records gifts of money, uḷi-uḷi etc. for the purpose of the daily worship, renovation, feeding of the ascetics and students of the college (khaṇḍika) belonging to the temple etc., after laying the feet of the temple-priest Gurusanna by the family of the queen Suggaladēvi and in 500 division on the occasion of Sūrya-grahaṇa, after laying the feet of the temple-priest by the family of the Chalukyas (of Kalyāṇa), his queen Suggaladēvi and records gifts of a number of tax like Hojjuku, Bilkode, Vaḍḍarāvaṇa, Vakkaladere, etc., to the same deity by the 300 Mahājanas of Sagara-nāḍu and Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara and the Mahānāḍu of Sagara-nāḍu (the latter having assembled in paḍ̣ada-mane-Ēgiri), and grants of land and a house-site as pūjārike to Bāmmu-jiya and Bīru-jiya, who were to convey the same in grant into a tāmra-śāsana as are referred to as the okkalu of the deity. Do.

cells.place: No. 3.
cells.date: Śaka 1335 (expired), 1336 (current), Vijaya, Āśvija, śu. 5, Thursday=1413 A.D., April 6, Wednesday (not Thursday).
cells.remarks: Records that on the first date, Chāvaḍayya, the governor of the Bārakūru-rājya, made a grant of 50 honnu of kāśi-gadyāṇa for the increase of the longevity and prosperity and for the destruction of the enemies of the emperor, for the amṛtapaḍi and other services and a perpetual lamp for the deities Nārāyaṇadēva, Rāma chandradēva, Gōpināthadēva and Viṭhaladēva, of the Kāṅgu-maṭha of Śivalli, worshipped by the disciples of Yādavēndratīrtha-śrīpāda. The grant is stated to have been made on the occasion of a solar eclipse, with the offering of the waters of ablution, on the west coast. Records that the grant was made of 50 honnu of kāśi-gadyāṇa, for the same purpose and the destruction of the enemies of the emperor, for the amṛtapaḍi service and a perpetual lamp for the deities worshipped by the disciples of Yādavēndratīrtha-śrīpāda (i.e., the second date), on the occasion of Uthāna-dōdaśi (i.e., the second date).

cells.location: Torapaḷḷi
cells.place: Rock called ‘Ruḍrapāda-gaḷabhaṇḍa’ in the village.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a dam named as Nañjarāja-sāgara across the river Ponnaiyāru, a tributary of the Bhadra-giri Trikūṭēśvarasvāmi on the banks of the river, Piṇākini by Nañjarājayya of Daḷavāyikshatriya-vaṃśa, and Bhāradvāja-gōtra, the younger brother of Koṇḍarāja and other sons of the chief of the Mysore family, Hosavūr. The construction was done with the blessings of his (Nañjarājayya’s) family preceptor, Svāmikēśvara Padmā-rasa-dēva and at the instance of his elder brother, the king, as an act of devotion to gods Mallikārjunadēva of Arala and Nañjuṇḍēśvara of Nañjuṇḍuḍu for the benefit and welfare of his family members viz., his father Nañjarājayya, his mother Liṅgāmbā-dēvamma and his younger brother Vīrarā-jayya and his own sons.

cells.date: Vikrama 1147, Māgha śu. 7, (week-day not given), Rēvatī = 1000 A.D., January 10. (The Vikrama year was current).
cells.remarks: Records that the maṇḍapa of the god Nīlakaṇṭha of Kālañjara was caused to be constructed by Śrīmūrti, the king's pre-ceptor. Records the gift of two pitchers (of water?) to the deity by the king's preceptor. The record is damaged probably as the writer. Also records the grant of two hala of land to the Sūtradhāra Arūma, the builder of the maṇḍapa. Cf. EI., 1935-36, pp. 93-94 and Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXI, pp. 163 ff. and plate.

cells.remarks: Damaged and obliterated. Mentions several persons like Vālhā, son of Mālhā, of Vālhā-gōtra, who constructed the shrine in the 16th century. The figure possibly of a lion of the Jōkkhama of Mahāvīra, is also found here. Records the perpetual choisance of Jāsati, wife of Vālhā, son of Lāhī, wife of Śāva, who was the son of Jāsakarī, wife of Nāyaka, Sha(Kah)nai. In characters of about the 11th century. The figures of a deer, the lāñchhana of Śāntinātha is also carved here.

cells.remarks: Late Contains a verse in anuṣṭubh metre in praise of Śiva describing him as the very embodiment of the three mūrttis i.e. Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva as the creator, protector and destroyer. Records that Sam° Dharaṇaka, the son of Kāmalade and Sam° Kumapāla and the grandson of Sam° Māṅgaṇa of Prāg-vāṭa family, belonging to the line of Sāḍā, Jāvada and others born of his wife Dhāraladevi, well as his elder brother Sam° Rātṇā and his wife Rākhā and their sons Lākhā, Mājā, Sōmā and Sāligā caused to be constructed at Rāṇapura a temple of Chaumukha (Chaturmukha) of Rīshabha, called Trailōkyadīpaka. The temple was consecrated by Sōmasundara-sūri of Bṛhadgaccha and Jayachandrasūri of Bṛhadgaccha-sūri-sūtradhāra. The construction was made by sūtradhāra Dēpāka, a Trāvaḍa. Cf. A.R. Ep., G.C. 1907-08, No. 1, p. 214; ff; Bhandarkar's List, No. 784.

cells.place: Below No. 3211 above.
cells.date: Vikrama 1181, Jyeṣṭha ba. 12, Wednesday = 1124 A.D., June 11
cells.remarks: States that Vasiṣṭha created a mountain called Nandi-vardhana alias Bhujangārbuda. On this mountain there was Vasiṣṭha a holy tīrtha of god Viṣṇu. A person named Sōḍhala, an ascetic, on the order of the king Pāṭṭa Nārāyaṇa after obtaining the permission from the brāhmaṇas at Grivda. The people of Grivda-Bhāga are stated to have made a number of grants including the village Pāṭi-kṣētra and Rudravāṭikā etc. and a grant of 50 drammas (given) to the god. At the end a reference is made to the work of renovation. Noticed in ibid.; Bhandarkar's List, No. 210.

cells.place: Bhuāwālā Tank. Slab in the northern wall.
cells.date: (1) Vikrama 1880(1) (2) 1876 A.D., Vikrama 1933 (3) 1878 A.D., July 20, Vikrama 1935
cells.remarks: Damaged. States that this tank which is called Bhuāwālā was first built in the reign of Shāh Jahān by a woman (name not mentioned) of Kaithī tribe, and was subsequently repaired (date not mentioned) by one Mīr Muḥammad, a money-lender (Sāhūkār) of Qasba Jhajjar on the first date. Further states that between the second and third dates, in the reign of the Queen, by the advice of Mr. G. N. Nox, Mr. E.F. Moon and Mr. M.P. D’Cruz, Deputy Commissioner, the tank was closed and repaired, the debris cleared, and fruit trees planted for beautifying the place. It also states that the cleaning and repair work was done by the contribution and donation received by the Municipal Committee. Lastly, it gives a list of donors and the amount of donation in each case.

cells.place: Tomb of 'Abdullāh Changāl. Slab over the doorway. (Do.)
cells.remarks: States that the saint 'Abdullāh Changāl was the first to propagate Islam successfully in this part. A few persons who had earlier come for the purpose having been killed by the infidels, the saint came in their wake and converted Shāj Bhoj to Islam. As the tombs of the saint and the martyrs were turned into ruins, the king Sulṭān ordered their reconstruction and also built a mosque on the north and a few rooms and also an inn for the travellers to the west. Text composed by Maḥmūd, son of Ḥusain. Cf. Ep. Ind. Mos., 1909-10, pp. 3-3, pl. I.

cells.location: Siruguppi
cells.place: Slab built into the wall of the bastion near the Śambhiliga-Svāmin temple. (Impression from Old Collection.)

cells.remarks: Nashk; Nāgarī: Records the construction of the bastion in the fort of Siruguppi by the local governor, Malik Muḥammad, son of Malik Raiḥān (barbārdār-i-khāṣṣ, Chief Custodian) of the fort of Adoni and the district (maḥallat) of Rāichūr and the city of Muḥammadpur and the Thānādār of the fort of Siruguppi. The date Shuhūr Sana 1018 seems to be the Hijri year for Shuhūr 1038. Published, Ep. Ind., Ar. Rep., 1953 and 1954, p. 42, pl. XIII (a). Cf. A. R. Ep., 1922-23, No. B. 676. For the text and the Kannaḍa versions, see ibid., Nos. B 676 and 674 respectively.
